nodes.text: Iterative Markovian Fitting (IMF) is a new procedure for solving Schrödinger Bridge problems that alternates between projecting onto the space of Markov processes and onto the reciprocal class (measures sharing the same bridge as the reference measure).
nodes.evidence: we introduce Iterative Markovian Fitting (IMF), a new procedure to compute SBs which alternates between projecting on the space of Markov processes and on the reciprocal class

nodes.text: Diffusion Schrödinger Bridge Matching (DSBM) is a numerical algorithm computing IMF iterates, where each iteration requires solving a simple regression problem in the spirit of Bridge and Flow Matching.
nodes.evidence: DSBM requires at each iteration solving a simple regression problem in the spirit of Bridge and Flow Matching

nodes.text: DSBM recovers various recent transport methods (Denoising Diffusion, Bridge Matching, Flow Matching) as special or limiting cases.
nodes.evidence: DSBM significantly improves over previous SB numerics and recovers as special/limiting cases various recent transport methods

nodes.text: Unlike DDMs and Flow Matching Models, which are not guaranteed to provide transports close to the optimal transport map, Schrödinger bridges compute stochastic dynamic mappings that recover entropy-regularized versions of OT.
nodes.evidence: DDMs and FMMs are not guaranteed to provide transports close to the OT map. In contrast, Schrödinger bridges (SBs) compute stochastic dynamic mappings which recover entropy-regularized versions of OT

nodes.text: In contrast to the Iterative Proportional Fitting (IPF) algorithm used by prior diffusion-based SB methods, IMF iterates always preserve the initial and terminal distributions.
nodes.evidence: Contrary to IPF, the IMF iterates always preserve the initial and terminal distributions

nodes.text: DSBM does not suffer from the time-discretization and 'forgetting' issues of previous Diffusion Schrödinger Bridge (DSB) techniques whose numerical errors accumulate over iterations.
nodes.evidence: does not suffer from the time-discretization and “forgetting” issues of previous DSB techniques

nodes.text: Flow Matching is recovered as the deterministic case of Bridge Matching / the Markovian projection in the limit of vanishing diffusion coefficient (sigma to 0).
nodes.evidence: Letting σ → 0, we recover Flow Matching models

nodes.text: DDMs can be seen as the first iteration of the Diffusion Schrödinger Bridge (DSB) algorithm.
nodes.evidence: In particular, DDMs can be seen as the first iteration of DSB.

nodes.text: The Markovian projection of a mixture-of-bridges path measure is shown to be the minimizer of the reverse KL divergence over Markov measures and to preserve all time marginals of the input measure.
nodes.evidence: M⋆ = argminM{KL(Π|M) : M ∈ M} ... for any t ∈ [0, T ], Mt⋆ = Πt

nodes.text: The Schrödinger Bridge is characterized as the unique path measure that simultaneously satisfies the initial and terminal constraints, is Markov, and lies in the reciprocal class of the reference measure Q.
nodes.evidence: the Schrödinger Bridge is the unique path measure which satisfies the initial and terminal conditions, is Markov and is in the reciprocal class of Q

nodes.text: A Pythagorean theorem holds for both Markovian and reciprocal projections, enabling a proof that the IMF sequence converges to the Schrödinger Bridge with KL(Pn|PSB) monotonically decreasing.

The IMF sequence admits a unique fixed point equal to the Schrödinger Bridge, with the sequence converging to it in KL divergence; this convergence was also shown in concurrent work by Peluchetti (2023).
nodes.evidence: the IMF sequence (Pn)n∈N admits a unique fixed point P⋆ = PSB, and limn→+∞ KL(Pn|P⋆) = 0

nodes.text: A naive numerical implementation of IMF performs poorly because the approximate minimization for computing the Markovian projection does not exactly enforce the terminal marginal constraint, motivating the practical DSBM refinements.
nodes.evidence: In practice, this algorithm performs poorly (see Figure 3), since the approximate minimization (10) for computing Mn+1 may not admit Mn+1 T = πT exactly
